q: When bodies are immersed in a liquid there is ____ in weight.
e: When bodies are immersed in a liquid there is loss in weight. Loss is what this statement is using.

q: This is because of a property of liquids called ____.
e: This is because of a property of liquids called buoyancy. The name used here is buoyancy.

q: Since buoyant force is directed upward, it is called ____.
e: Buoyant force is the upward push of the fluid, equal to the weight of the displaced fluid. Since buoyant force is directed upward, it is called upward thrust.

q: Archimedes' principle states that the upward thrust acting on a body which is immersed in a liquid is equal to the ____ of the liquid displaced by the body.
e: Archimedes' principle: the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced. Archimedes' principle states that the upward thrust acting on a body which is immersed in a liquid is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced by the body.

q: Archimedes' principle is true not only for liquids but also for ____.
e: Archimedes' principle: the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced. Archimedes' principle is true not only for liquids but also for gases.

q: The weight of a body when it is immersed in a liquid is called ____.
e: The weight of a body when it is immersed in a liquid is called apparent weight. The name used here is apparent weight.

q: It is less than the actual weight of the body because of ____ of the liquid acting on it.
e: It is less than the actual weight of the body because of upward thrust of the liquid acting on it. Upward thrust is what this statement is using.

q: A body will float in a liquid (fluid) if the upward thrust acting on it is ____ to its weight.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. A body will float in a liquid (fluid) if the upward thrust acting on it is equal to its weight.

q: If the weight of the body is greater than the upward thrust, the body will ____.
e: If the weight of the body is greater than the upward thrust, the body will sink. Sink is what this statement is using.

q: If the weight is smaller than the upward thrust, the body will ____ up to the surface.
e: If the weight is smaller than the upward thrust, the body will rise up to the surface. Rise is what this statement is using.

q: Since the body is in equilibrium, the net force acting on it is ____.
e: Since the body is in equilibrium, the net force acting on it is zero. Zero is what this statement is using.

q: According to Eq. (3.8), the ratio of the densities is equal to the ratio of the immersed volume to the ____ of the whole body.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. According to Eq. (3.8), the ratio of the densities is equal to the ratio of the immersed volume to the volume of the whole body.
